clue.text: Match-box which sets a precedent

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: Someone asks which box of matches set a legal precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose ruling then guides later judgments.

clue.text: Hero of story, in Rugby terms

definitions.text: Hero of story, in Rugby terms

parts.words: Hero of story, in Rugby terms
parts.note: reads like a rugby player described in the game's jargon, but points to the boy hero of a Victorian school novel set at Rugby School

explanation.surface: A rugby star is described in the jargon of the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby here is the English public school, setting of Thomas Hughes's novel of schooldays, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Hughes's Victorian schoolboy novel set at Rugby School.

clue.text: Passed, with relish, on board this vessel

definitions.text: Passed, with relish, on board this vessel

parts.words: Passed, with relish, on board this vessel
parts.note: sounds like a ship's passenger enjoying the voyage, but describes a jug of gravy handed round the dinner table

explanation.surface: Someone sails past happily aboard some ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' is a condiment and 'board' the dining table; the 'vessel' is a jug, not a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravy jug is handed along the table with its sauce on board, a dinner-table vessel.

clue.text: More than eight, less than 22 in this town

definitions.text: More than eight, less than 22 in this town

parts.words: More than eight, less than 22 in this town
parts.note: the town's name is one letter longer than the word for a rowing eight and one letter shorter than the solution to 22 down

explanation.surface: A number puzzle about some town's population or count.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing eight is a CREW; add a letter for the town, and add one more (L) to get the yarn at 22 down. Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheshire railway junction town sits between the boat's team and the embroidery yarn by spelling.

clue.text: Maker of observations — on gamesmanship, etc

explanation.surface: Someone notes down how players bend the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter wrote the humorous book Gamesmanship (and Lifemanship etc); 'S. Potter' is his name as a byline.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks out for things, such as an aircraft watcher; also the initial and surname of Stephen Potter, author of Gamesmanship.

clue.text: We hear you are hiding safe for money-lender

indicators.note: the outer pair of sounded letters conceal the next piece inside them
signals that the words 'you are' are to be taken by how they sound when spoken, as two letters

parts.note: said quickly, 'you are' sounds like the letters U and R
sure means safe, certain, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: Someone claims a person is concealing a strongbox of cash for a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lends money at extortionate interest rates.

clue.text: Craft found briefly in Sussex and Essex

definitions.text: Craft found briefly in Sussex and Essex

parts.words: Craft found briefly in Sussex and Essex
parts.note: the abbreviation for this vessel, SS, appears in the names of both English counties, so the craft is found there in brief form

explanation.surface: A boat has been spotted in two English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' means abbreviated: SS, the prefix for a steam-powered vessel, ends both county names. Sussex and Essex are English counties.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven by steam power, abbreviated SS.

clue.text: Dressing tailless bird

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, as a creature without its tail

parts.note: robing is putting on robes, dressing

explanation.surface: A bird without a tail is used as a dressing or stuffing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red-breasted songbird.

clue.text: Further left, up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same going up as going down, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Moving further left, then up and down, as in directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is the political colour of the left, so more red is more left-wing.

clue.text: Remarks not directed at players as team enters

indicators.note: the team word goes inside the little word 'as', as a team entering

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: Comments are made to the audience while a team comes onto the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre, these remarks are spoken to the audience, not to the other actors ('players').
explanation.definitionFit: Stage remarks spoken to the audience, unheard by the other characters.

clue.text: Get doctor to treat a black eye

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
to use someone is to treat them, as in 'used badly'

explanation.surface: A patient with a black eye is told to see a doctor for treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bruised swollen eye, so called for its shape and colour.

clue.text: Rest of natives here ?

parts.note: natives are a classic British breed of shellfish, and a bed is where they lie and rest

explanation.surface: Asks where the remainder of the local people are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natives' are Whitstable or Colchester shellfish; 'rest' is lying in bed, not 'the remainder'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabed area where shellfish are bred or grow naturally.

clue.text: Seated, having had to stand repeatedly

definitions.text: Seated, having had to stand repeatedly

parts.words: Seated, having had to stand repeatedly
parts.note: a politician stands for office again and wins back the seat

explanation.surface: Someone finally sits down after standing up several times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seated' means given a parliamentary seat; 'stand' means run for election, and 'repeatedly' means again.
explanation.definitionFit: Returned to office in a further vote, holding the seat once more.

clue.text: Some churchman's environment

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: A clergyman's surroundings are described.
explanation.walkthrough: The text held had a stray extra "man's"; the printed clue runs churchMAN'S Environment.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's house, typically of a Scottish Presbyterian clergyman, is where he lives.

clue.text: It's largely untrue

parts.note: a big lie is untrue on a large scale

explanation.surface: A claim is dismissed as mostly false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like 'mostly' but means 'in a big way': a huge lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a gross falsehood, a really big fib.

clue.text: Rook pie, for example ? Not altogether

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
a pie is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pie made of rooks counts, answered 'not entirely'.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook pie is a traditional English country dish; here the rook is the chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Done bit by bit, in stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Place in society ball

definitions.meaning: a round solid body, a globe

explanation.definitionFit: A social realm or circle; also a round globe-shaped body.

clue.text: One enters study with head for preparation

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the joined words, as one entering

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
a ness is a headland
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone takes up studying, with a head start, as they prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland (Loch Ness aside), as in Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prepared and ready for something.

clue.text: Top -liner reorganized multinational bureau

indicators.note: the letters of the hyphenated word are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A top performer has been restructured in an international agency.
explanation.definitionFit: The international police organisation that coordinates cooperation between national forces.

clue.text: Many dwell on this anagram made by setter

indicators.note: the clue states outright that the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter claims to have made a well-known anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town, which people live along.

clue.text: Relations with unions — what can consumers do ?

parts.note: TU is trade union
C is short for cum, Latin for 'with'
kin are relations, family

explanation.surface: Asks about labour relations and what shoppers can do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumers' are eaters, not shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: To start eating heartily, a phrasal verb for eating with gusto.

clue.text: Kettle's handle used by Cook, for one

definitions.meaning: the title of ... Kettle, a fictional sea hero of adventure stories
James Cook, the explorer, is an example of a naval officer of this rank

explanation.surface: A kettle handle is used by someone cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kettle was a popular fictional sea captain; 'handle' means title.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's commander or naval rank: Kettle's title and the rank of explorer James Cook.

clue.text: King's taking in learner, for example

definitions.text: King's taking in learner, for example

parts.words: King's taking in learner, for example
parts.note: King's at Cambridge is an example of a place admitting students

explanation.surface: A king takes in a learner, perhaps as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's' is King's College, Cambridge, not a monarch; 'learner' is a student.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution of higher education admitting students, such as King's at Cambridge.

clue.text: It doesn't sound like kind of yarn

definitions.text: It doesn't sound like kind of yarn

parts.words: It doesn't sound like kind of yarn
parts.note: the embroidery thread is pronounced like the word meaning not kind, heartless

explanation.surface: A story is said not to be the friendly sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' is the adjective, and 'yarn' a thread, not a tale; the word sounds like 'cruel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loosely twisted worsted wool thread used for embroidery.

clue.text: If keeping sides apart, 'e produces a gun

indicators.note: the two side letters hold the next piece between them

parts.note: the sides right and left, R and L, set apart
taken as written
the dropped-h 'e gives the letter E

explanation.surface: A Cockney-sounding man produces a gun while keeping two parties apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled firearm with a grooved bore.

clue.text: Net result if rising allowed to succeed

indicators.note: in a down clue the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A good result is obtained if success is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' looks like a final sum, as in net result, but it names a fine mesh fabric; in a down clue 'rising' reads a word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh fabric, as in filet lace.

clue.text: Wordsworth's little " flower .that shall be mine "

definitions.text: Wordsworth's little " flower .that shall be mine "

parts.words: Wordsworth's little " flower .that shall be mine "
parts.note: quotes Wordsworth's poem to a small yellow spring flower that he claimed as his own

explanation.surface: A line of Wordsworth's about a small flower he will own.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem 'To the Small Celandine' says 'There's a flower that shall be mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow spring wildflower of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Leader of House in French resort for recess

indicators.note: the leading letter sits inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The Leader of the House goes on holiday to a French resort during the recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recess' looks like a parliamentary holiday, but it is an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow alcove in a wall, for a statue or ornament.

clue.text: Glutton could be wine-lover

indicators.note: the hyphenated phrase could become another word if its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A greedy eater may turn out to be fond of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The glutton is another name for this voracious weasel-family animal.

clue.text: Penny each, perhaps

parts.note: goods priced at a penny apiece are inexpensive

explanation.surface: A price tag reading a penny apiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Low in price; a penny each is a bargain rate.

clue.text: Though insignificant by itself it was novel

definitions.text: Though insignificant by itself it was novel

parts.words: Though insignificant by itself it was novel
parts.note: alone the word means small or unimportant, yet it begins famous novel titles such as Dickens's tale of Dorrit and Alcott's Women

explanation.surface: Something unimportant on its own was once new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' means a book, not 'new': Little Dorrit and Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Small and unimportant; also the first word of novel titles like Little Women.

clue.text: Change of -direction ? Right — several moving south

indicators.note: one letter of the word is taken out and put back elsewhere in it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A navigator changes course, turning right with several ships heading south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the S of SEVERAL along to make EVERSAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-around, going back the opposite way.
